title: "Sparklines in a table"
description: "vtable() renders a data frame with a list-column of vectors as per-row sparklines; gt_vsparkline() does the same inside a gt table."
categories: [Statistical]
image: figs/sparkline-vtable.png
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("_helper.R")
```

A metrics table usually shows where each number ended: revenue this month,
errors this week. It rarely shows how the number got there. A sparkline column
adds that path without adding a chart. vellumplot builds it two ways, depending
on whether you want a plain rendered table or a live `gt` one.

`vtable()` takes a data frame where one or more columns are **list-columns of
numeric vectors**, and draws the whole thing as a single vector scene: ordinary
columns become text, the list-columns become per-row sparklines. `spark` maps
each such column to a shape.

```{r}
set.seed(1)
metrics <- data.frame(
  metric = c("Revenue", "Users", "Latency", "Errors"),
  latest = format(c(4213, 18402, 128, 37), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE),
  change = c("+4.2%", "+1.1%", "-8ms", "-12%")
)
metrics$trend  <- lapply(1:4, function(i) cumsum(rnorm(24)))
metrics$volume <- lapply(1:4, function(i) rpois(20, 6))

p <- vtable(metrics, spark = list(trend = "line", volume = "bar"), row_height = 8)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
vg(p, "sparkline-vtable")
```

Every row's `trend` is a line sparkline and every row's `volume` a bar one,
drawn from the vectors in those columns. The result is one PNG (or SVG, or PDF):
no per-cell image files, no HTML.

## The same thing in a gt table

If you already build tables with [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), `gt_vsparkline()`
adds a sparkline column while keeping gt's own formatting and theming. It embeds
each chart as inline SVG through `plot_svg()`, so this table is live HTML on the
page, not a screenshot.

```{r}
#| output: asis
library(gt)
set.seed(1)
svc <- data.frame(metric = c("Revenue", "Users", "Latency", "Errors"))
svc$trend  <- lapply(1:4, function(i) cumsum(rnorm(24)))
svc$volume <- lapply(1:4, function(i) rpois(20, 6))

gt(svc) |>
  tab_header(title = "Service metrics") |>
  gt_vsparkline(trend, type = "line") |>
  gt_vsparkline(volume, type = "bar", color = "#4682b4")
```

`plot_svg()` is the piece doing the work in both the inline-text examples and
this table: it turns any vellumplot object into a self-contained SVG string. The
same call embeds a chart in a
[reactable](https://glin.github.io/reactable/) or
[DT](https://rstudio.github.io/DT/) cell, or anywhere else that accepts an HTML
fragment.
